messages.subject: editing PCA plot and exporting 3D plots
parts:
Hello,
I've successfully been able to generate my Generalize Procrustes Analysis for this dataset and run a Principle Components Analysis. However, when I try to export the 3D plot of the GPA$coords data, it pops up as an RGL tab and not within the Plots for RStudio; when I've tried publishing it as a .png, I got a blank .png. I've been able to save the PCA plot as an image, but can't figure out how to add specimen labels (or even just 1, 2, 3,... since I know what order the data rows are in) to the PCA plot that is generated.
I've attached both my .csv file and my R file.
I know these are both probably easy things to do, but I'm at a loss and very time I try using ggplot on the data, it returns errors. I'm very new to R and need all the help I can get!
Thanks!!
-Hale

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] editing PCA plot and exporting 3D plots
parts:
Hi Hale, 

You can try rgl.snapshot(), or maybe google for alternative ways.

For adding labels you could do something like this using plot():
plot(PCA_scap, main = "PCA_scap")
text(PCA_scap$x[,1], PCA_scap$x[,2], 1:12, pos = 4)

or use geom_text() using ggplot. There are many guides online on this, this is one of them: https://r-graph-gallery.com/275-add-text-labels-with-ggplot2.html. Welcome to ggplot, it can be challenging to learn (even for people with R experience). 

Usually for most errors I do not recognize or for many things involving ggplot, I just google my error or issue and after a bit of searching I can usually figure it out. All I am saying is google or stackexchange are awesome resources, especially for beginners!

Best,
Bryan
